      "label": "HazardConsequence",
      "name": "Confined explosion",
      "node_id": "H1",
      "node_type": "HazardConsequence",
      "evidence": "The report section is titled \"June 20, 2017 Explosion.\" It states that the CSB determined reactive, unstable chemicals exploded when workers tried to drain chemically treated liquid from odorizer equipment. On June 20, 2017, \"the MP odorizer exploded less than five minutes after the draining operation had begun,\" and \"a portion of the MP chamber struck and fatally injured the field supervisor.\" The analysis further states that the vessels were sealed and that the explosions were likely caused by uncontrolled chemical reactions resulting in violent rupture of the odorizer.",
      "explanation": "The main accident mechanism analyzed is a reactive chemical explosion occurring inside a sealed odorizer vessel, causing vessel rupture and projectile hazards. This is best classified as a confined explosion because the hazardous phenomenon was an internal explosion/overpressure event within enclosed equipment, not a vapor cloud, dust, fire, or toxic release event.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
